title: Conveyor project pack (.conveyor/project.json)
description: What Conveyor knows of one project. conveyor/lib/pack.sh checks a pack against this file with jq, so it may use only the keywords pack.sh lists; a field with a default may be left out.

plugin.description: The plugin this project runs (plan section 7): one commit it is pinned to (commit), or the plugin's newest release or its main as they move (follow), never both.

follow.description: Each machine takes the plugin's newest published release (releases) or its pushed main (main, for testing changes before they are released) once it passes its check (docs/setup.md, Following releases or main, or pinning a commit).

name.description: Whose yes a visible change needs, and the word an approval line may hold.

built.description: Built and merged, waiting for the owner's deploy: never picked.

followup.description: The label of the follow-ups Conveyor files.

type.description: The type label a filed follow-up carries.

priorities.description: The priority labels, most urgent first.

nonProductAreas.description: Area labels whose issues are not product work.

productPaths.description: Path prefixes of product code: a change under one needs the owner's yes when it is visible.

pipelineFiles.description: The files, and the folders (each file under one), that are how cards are built, reviewed, fixed, tested, landed or pushed, as paths from the repository root: a follow-up whose finding names one is filed held, and built only once the owner releases it.

command.description: Run in a card's worktree before the card lands.

control.description: Test files, as paths from the repository root, that tell a broken machine from a broken main (conveyor/README.md, The test step's verdicts). When a card's failing cases fail on main too, the ones of these that passed before with main's content run beside them on the same slot. When no test passed before with main's content, as with a test command that records no passes, all of these run. When every control that runs fails, the failure is the machine's: no fix card opens, and the loop picks no card until the failing files pass again. Empty, or none of these runs: a failure on main is main's unless its test file passed before with the same inputs.

list.description: How test.command takes the list of the test files a card's change touches, in a card's run: args (each path added at the end), placeholder (the paths in place of {files} in test.command), env (CONVEYOR_TEST_FILES, one path a line), runner (go test: the package of each *_test.go file in place of ./...; cargo test: --test <name> for each tests/<name>.rs) or none (it takes no list: the whole suite runs). A change that touches shared setup or config, or a file with no test found for it, runs the whole suite (no path given). Not set: the command is given no list.

fileCommand.description: Runs one test file, its path from the repository root as its first argument and in CONVEYOR_TEST_FILE. When set, the bug-card check runs each test file of the change with it, one at a time, in place of test.command.

checkCommand.description: The project's checks (a lint, shellcheck and the like), run in a card's worktree after each build, fix and rebase session and at the start of its Test step; exit 0 passes. A failure goes to a fix session with the output, before any review or test, and does not use up the card's one test-fix round. The result is kept for the tree it ran on, so the Test step on that tree does not run it again. Not set: no such check.

cardFiles.description: With the rule Whole suite in a card off, the most test files a bug card's check runs of those of its change: of more, the files that failed most recently in a test step first, then the rest in the test map's order. The check's result says how many were left out. A card's own run is not limited by it: it runs the test files its change adds or changes, or, with none, 5 of those linked to its change.

fileBudget.description: Ignored: no test file has a CPU budget. doctor says so once while the pack holds it.

splitAllowance.description: The start-up CPU seconds allowed for each test file a split adds, when the check of an Optimize card cannot measure them (conveyor/README.md, Test file times): the files of a split may take, summed, the old file's CPU seconds on record plus this for each file the split adds. The check first measures it, by a run of a file the split adds with no case selected.

files.description: Settings of one test file, by its path from the repository root (conveyor/README.md, The test files in the snapshot). budget: ignored, as fileBudget is. slowOnPurpose: the reason the file is slow on purpose, one line; no CPU test rule (usual) files an issue about such a file. Set and cleared with `conveyor.sh test-settings`. cardMode and wholeOnly, of a meta-runner (a test file that starts other test files), are read by the project's card test command (this project's .conveyor/test-changed.sh): cardMode, the NAME=VALUE that makes the file run its own checks with a stub in place of the files it starts, which a card's test step runs it with; wholeOnly: true, a card's test step does not run it, the nightly whole test does. A meta-runner with neither fails a card's test step.

slower.description: When the snapshot's tests part names a test file slower than its usual: its CPU seconds in each of its last runs card runs are over its usual (the median of its runs before those) by more than share (0.25: 25%), and at least minRuns runs of it are on record.

slowIssues.description: Files nothing: the test rules (rules) replace the "Slow test" issues it filed.

rules.description: The test rules (conveyor/README.md, Test rules): each files one issue about a test file that meets its limit, behind one switch and the guards. Set with `conveyor.sh testrules`; `conveyor.sh testrules preview` lists what they match now and files nothing.

on.description: The switch of every rule. false (the default): no rule files anything.

perDay.description: The most issues the rules file in one day; the rest wait for the next day.

maxOpen.description: The most issues of the rules open at one time.

quietDays.description: The days after the last issue filed for a file closes in which no issue is filed for that file.

burst.description: true (the default): a pass that matches more files than perDay files nothing and puts one line in "Needs you".

list.description: The rules, in the order they are read: a file two rules match is filed by the first.

measure.description: budget: ignored, a rule that matches nothing (no test file has a CPU budget); doctor says so once while the pack holds one; usual: CPU seconds over limit times its usual (the median of its runs before the last runs); clock: clock seconds over limit times CPU seconds, with at least minClock clock seconds; flaky: at least limit flaky entries of its cases in the last days days; failed: at least limit failed test steps in it in the last days days.

runs.description: The card test runs in a row that each meet the limit (usual, clock).

minRuns.description: The least count of the file's card test runs on record.

days.description: flaky and failed: the days counted.

minClock.description: clock: the least clock seconds of a run.

survey.description: The monthly test-speed survey: on the first day of each month, in the hour surveyHour, `serve` files one issue whose card runs each test file alone, records its clock and CPU seconds, and rewrites the slowest lists and the survey report. false: none is filed.

firstSurvey.description: The answer setup saved to its question "Run a first test-speed survey now?": true, setup filed one survey issue; false, none. Unset, setup asks it and changes nothing until it is answered; once saved, it is not asked again, and `setup --survey yes|no` answers it again.

surveyHour.description: The machine's quietest hour, local time (0 to 23), in which the monthly test-speed survey's issue is filed on the 1st, and the only hour in which its card is picked: 3 is 03:00 to 03:59.

map.description: The test map a card's list of tests (test.list) is read against: which test files cover which source files. Not set: the map setup makes with the project's coverage tool, .conveyor/test-map.json, refreshed by a whole run on main that passes when it is due (mapAge). off: no map; a card's tests are found by name. A path from the repository root: a map the project keeps itself, a JSON object {"<source file>": ["<test file>", ...]} or lines of areas as .conveyor/engine-areas.json holds them, never made or refreshed by Conveyor.

mapAge.description: How many commits the made test map may be behind the commit a whole run on main tests before that run makes it again.

main.description: The whole test, run by the loop in a worktree of the default branch, never by a card: at most once an hour (once a day with mainAt), when the branch has moved since its last run. Each failed case is run again alone 3 times: one that passes every time goes to the flaky-test record; the cases that fail alone file one issue naming them, their failure lines and the commits since the last pass. None: no such run.

mainAt.description: The time of day, HH:MM in the machine's local time, after which the whole test on main (main) runs once a day, in place of at most once an hour. None: at most once an hour.

full.description: The full test suite, run on the default branch from the Board: its Run full test suite, and Push landed, which pushes what landed only once it passes. Each failed case is run again alone and judged (flaky, a fix card, or declined). None: both buttons are off.

wholeCommands.description: Test runners that run the whole suite when no case is named, as paths from the repository root: the command guard refuses one in a card's build or fix session unless the command names a case (conveyor/README.md, When a full test run is allowed).

report.description: How Conveyor reads each test file's clock seconds from the test runner's own report, for a test command that prints no `TESTRUN sec` lines (conveyor/README.md, Test file times). Setup writes it from the runner it finds in test.command: runner, the runner found; format, how to read its report (none: Conveyor cannot read what the command writes now); path, the report file or folder, from the repository root (none: the file Conveyor names when env or args has <file>, else the command's own output); env, environment variables Conveyor sets at each run to ask the runner for its report, each value added after the variable's own, <file> in it the report file Conveyor names and <mochatimes> the path of Conveyor's mocha timer; args, the words Conveyor adds at the end of the test command at each run for the same, with <file> as in env; option, the runner's report option that would give Conveyor the times, when format is none.

coverage.description: The coverage report a card's test command already writes, from which the card's test step lists the changed lines no test reached (conveyor/README.md, Changed lines no test reached): format, the report's format; path, the report file or a folder of report files, from the repository root. A lead for the reviewer: it never fails a run, and Conveyor starts no other run for it. None: no such list.

changed.description: The script that runs the tests a change touches, as a path from the repository root: the command guard refuses it a second time in one card session.

sessionBudget.description: The CPU seconds of test commands (node --test, a *.test.sh, pytest, vitest or jest) one card build or fix session may use: once the session's test commands have used more, the command guard refuses its next test command (conveyor/README.md, The session test budget). The card's test step still runs the tests. 3600 CPU s is an estimate, not a measurement: the 95th percentile (3596.5 CPU s), rounded up, of 175 logged sessions' test commands, each given its test files' CPU seconds from other runs' test steps, or its clock seconds where none was recorded.

patterns.description: The project's test files, as globs of paths from the repository root (docs/configuration.md, How test files are found): * and ? match in one folder name, ** across folders, a glob ending in / matches each file under such a folder, and a glob matches at any depth unless it starts with /. A path one of them matches is a test file, never product code. Set, it replaces the default.

inline.description: The kinds of tests written inside product files (docs/configuration.md, Tests inside product files), one entry a kind: files, the globs of the files it is found in (as tests.patterns); start, a POSIX extended regular expression that starts a test block; end, "braces" (the block ends where the brackets opened after start close, or at a ; before any opens) or a regular expression the block ends on; has, a regular expression one line of the block must match to make it a test (none: every block is one). A bug card's check runs such a file with its new test blocks and without the rest of the change. The pack's entries are added to the default ones; an entry of the same name replaces the default's.

linkFromMain.description: Worktree-relative paths linked from the main checkout into each card's worktree: the dependency folders its tests need, such as node_modules. Setup proposes the ignored dependency folders it finds in the main checkout while this is empty and worktree.setup is unset.

setup.description: A command run once in each new worktree of the project, from its top, after the links of linkFromMain and before its build and tests: the install of its dependencies, such as npm ci, for a project whose dependency folders are not linked (for example when a card may change the lockfile). When it fails, the card is blocked with its last lines. None: nothing runs.

env.description: Variables set for the engine's push.

landAs.description: The rule Land as, until the control record sets it (docs/configuration.md, Land as): main pushes main to defaultBranch; pr pushes main to the branch conveyor/landing and keeps one pull request open from it into defaultBranch, which closes the cards' issues when it is merged.

check.description: Whether, before each push of main, the test files the test map and the links give the landings since the last push run, each alone, and a file that fails holds the push. Off, a push runs no test first. The control record's pushCheck (conveyor.sh control push-check on|off, or the Rules tab) wins over it.

allowed.description: Default models for the builder and the reviewer, by the program that runs them: the first for a seat is its default. They limit nothing the control record sets (a CLI installed on the host and a model it has registered: docs/configuration.md, Models). With none set, the project follows the models the CLIs report: Codex's from its models cache, Claude's the built-in list.

codex-builder.description: Builder models Codex runs (conveyor/README.md, Codex builder), each a model name as models.allowed.codex names one.

opencode.description: The OpenCode models the builder (conveyor/README.md, OpenCode builder), the reviewer and the judge may run on, each opencode:<provider>/<model> (OpenCode's provider/model, as `opencode models` lists it); a name of another shape is never offered or run.

claudeProxy.description: The API proxy Claude card sessions run through, as its roles set: its base URL and the NAME of the environment variable that holds its key (never the key). toolSearch is ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH for a base URL that is not api.anthropic.com (true when left out). The host file's claudeProxy, when it names one, is used instead.

roles.description: Each role's route: proxy (the default for a role not named): its Claude sessions run through it. fallback: they run on the subscription login, and one whose login fails before any turn runs again through the proxy. subscription: they never run through it.

prices.description: Your model prices, added models and aliases, by model ID. Prices are $ per million tokens: input, output and cacheRead together, and cacheWrite (a 5-minute cache write; with none, 1.25 times input); they win over the Board's built-in price of that model, and price a model it has not got. name is the model's display name, provider the group an added model shows in, aliases the other model IDs that mean the model. Set on the Board (Rules, Model prices) or with conveyor.sh prices.

log.description: The ruling log, a path under the user's home (~/...).

checks.description: Extra check commands run before a card lands, repo-relative: the list itself, or an object whose run is that list and whose progress is a command, run from the repo root, printing the current or most recent check run as one JSON object (nothing when there has been none) for the Board and /units: {name, sha, started, ended (null while it runs), result (pass, fail or null), lanes: [{name, state (queued, running, passed, failed or reused), started, sec}]}, times in UTC ISO.

commit.description: The commit trailers of a card's commit: a card writes its own in <worktree>.trailers.

trailers.description: Trailers required by condition: when a path the change adds matches when (an ERE), the commit carries a token line; ask is the sentence the build prompt gives for it.

forbid.description: Trailer tokens a card may not write (Co-Authored-By never may).

areas.description: Area rule files a card is given, by path glob (plan section 10).

foreman.description: The Foreman's model and effort (plan section 11b), and when its watcher wakes it for a waiting card.

waitWake.description: Minutes a card waits for main to change, or on another card, before the Foreman's watcher wakes it (watch-conveyor.sh); it wakes again, "still waiting", after each further waitWake minutes of the same wait.

review.description: How the card review is asked.

proof.description: any: any proof that can be reproduced makes a finding; real: a finding's proof must happen with what the project really runs, else it is an UNPROVEN line (a security finding is exempt).

rereviewWhole.description: The review after a fix of review findings reviews the fix's diff and the findings it was told to fix, not the whole change again, unless the fix touches more than this percent of the change's added and removed lines: then it reviews the whole change. 0 reviews the whole change after every fix that changes a line.

wording.description: A file of the project, from its checkout's root, holding the wording /conveyor-belt:review gives Codex, in place of the plugin's conveyor/rules/review.md: a `# adversarial` section and a `# review` section (conveyor.sh wording).

auto.description: /conveyor-belt:auto, where the Foreman decides the owner's open decisions for them (conveyor.sh auto).

reserved.description: What is never decided for the owner: an open decision whose question, recommended option or options hold one of these words or phrases (in any case) waits for the owner.

standing.description: The standing kinds of routine yes the Foreman takes without asking, each logged in the ruling log (source standing): asked-fix (a fix the owner asked for is filed and released at once), review-followup (a follow-up of a card the owner approved that only finishes or corrects that card's change is released; the engine releases one whose finding names only files of its parent card's change), release-check (a failed check in a release the owner asked for gets one fix card, then the release goes on), fixed-block (a card whose block a landed fix removed gets Depends on: #<fix> and retry --fresh). Each kind is off until the owner turns it on (the Board's Rules tab).

privacy.description: How the privacy check (conveyor/privacy/check.sh) gates every GitHub write the engine and the Board make.

mode.description: public: a hit keeps the text local and posts nothing, and so does a terms file the host file names that cannot be read (the terms file is optional); private: a hit is a warning and the text is posted.

landBatch.description: At most this many cards that are ready to land and share files land together, on one test run (1: each lands alone).

parse.description: After any merge at landing, each file the merge changed is checked to parse before any test runs: a glob (its * matches a / too) to the command run on each file it matches, the file's path added after it. These add to the engine's own (*.js and *.mjs: node --check, *.sh: bash -n, *.json: jq empty, *.py: python3 -m py_compile); one of the same glob replaces it.

tunables.description: The loop's timings, in seconds (waitLimitMin: in minutes).

poll.description: A loop with a free builder slot looks for an issue at least this often.

idle.description: serve with nothing in flight and nothing to pick looks again after this.

stuck.description: health lists an open card with no new line and no output for this long; a build, fix, rebase or review with no output, file change or commit for this long is ended and runs once more, and a second stall blocks the card.

sessionStuck.description: health lists a card whose session (build, fix, rebase) has had no output for this long, when that is sooner than stuck.

caseStuck.description: health lists a card whose test step has one case running for this long: the ceiling of one case.

waitLimitMin.description: health lists a card that has waited on other cards for more than this many minutes in total.

sample.description: A sample is taken at most this often.

live.description: A running step's live record is brought up to date this often.

closeWait.description: After a push, GitHub is given this long to show a landed card's issue closed.

pushRetry.description: A failed push is tried again at least this often.

reviewPause.description: A review that ended with no verdict, and a build, fix, rebase or review ended for no progress, runs once more after this pause.

apiPause.description: A session the model API refused (403 Cloudflare, 429, 5xx, overloaded, connection reset) runs again after 1, 2, 4 and 8 times this, and no new card starts for 5 times this. A card blocked by a session that stopped before any work gets a check session at most this often.

limitTtl.description: The weekly limit reading is asked for again once the last asking is this old (0: at every asking).

limitOld.description: A weekly limit reading older than this is no reading.

testActionTimeout.description: A test action's session (conveyor.sh testaction) is ended once it has run this long, and its record says timed out.
